title: South Carolina, April 1775 to Cowpens, 17 January 1781
subtitle: Who fought where, who won, and who held the towns and forts, month by month

about: Dates and results come from the South Carolina Archives list of actions (Lipscomb), the National Park Service's Cowpens timeline, the American Battlefield Trust's battle pages and Wikipedia's articles on the actions, each checked against at least one other. Nothing here has been checked by a historian.

A clash is drawn in the colour and shape of the side that won it. A grey diamond is a fight no source scores as a win. A dagger marks a result or a date on which the sources disagree; both readings are on the Hypotheses sheet and none has been chosen yet.

Positions are marked by the best source read: a marker, an encyclopedia or park coordinate, or a point taken from a modern map. Each carries its precision in metres; a lost battle site is marked low. 1777 and 1778 are flagged as gaps in the list.

modern.about: Today's ground: the US Geological Survey's topographic base map, with roads, towns, streams, contours and hill shading. It is streamed from the USGS while it is on screen, so it needs a connection.
modern.name: USGS Topo base map

gaps.text: 1777: no actions in the South Carolina Archives list. A gap in the list, not proof of a quiet year; the Cherokee cession of 20 May 1777 is the one event read for it.
1778: one entry only (the capture of privateers at Charleston, 19 Jun). The sources read do not say who took them, so no clash is drawn.

phases.title: Where things stood at the end of 1777

playback.page_title: South Carolina, 1775 to Cowpens: an orientation

opening.label: Before the first shots
opening.text: South Carolina, early 1775: the royal government still stands. Press play and the fights come onto the map month by month, each drawn for the side that won it.

sides.name: British Crown forces (British and German troops)

events.name: Charleston: arms and powder seized
events.text: Patriot leaders carry off the arms stored in the State House attic and powder from two outlying magazines, without a fight. [T01]

events.name: Fort Charlotte surrenders
events.text: Major James Mayson takes the royal fort on the Savannah River in the Council of Safety's name; the garrison gives it up. [T02]

events.name: Fort Johnson taken
events.text: South Carolina troops under Colonel Isaac Motte walk into Fort Johnson, whose guns the royal navy had just disabled. [T03]

events.name: Ninety Six: Savage's Old Field
events.text: Loyalists surround Major Williamson's Patriot stockade near Ninety Six. Neither side wins; a truce ends the first bloodshed in the state. [T04]

events.name: Great Cane Brake
events.text: Colonel Thomson's rangers and militia surprise a Loyalist camp on the Reedy River and take over a hundred prisoners. [T05]

events.name: Snow Campaign
events.text: Richardson's militia, thousands strong, march through the backcountry; the Loyalist leaders are seized or scattered and snow ends the campaign. [T06]

events.name: Sullivan's Island (Fort Sullivan)
events.text: The unfinished palmetto fort at the harbour mouth drives off the British fleet. [T07]

events.name: Breach Inlet
events.text: Clinton's troops on Long Island find the inlet too deep to wade and cannot cross to Sullivan's Island. [T08]

events.name: Cherokee War begins
events.text: The Cherokee strike the western settlements; the war runs to the treaty of 20 May 1777. [T09]

events.name: Esseneca (Seneca Old Town)
events.text: A Loyalist and Cherokee force ambushes Williamson's column near the Cherokee town of Esseneca; Pickens arrives and the Patriots recover. [T10]

events.name: Tamassee and the Ring Fight
events.text: Pickens and 25 men form a ring against a Cherokee attack near Tamassee until relief arrives; Williamson then burns the town. [T11]

events.name: Capture of privateers, Charleston
events.text: The only action the Archives list gives for 1778. Neither the list nor any source read says who took which ships. [T12]

events.name: Port Royal Island (Beaufort)
events.text: Moultrie's Continentals and militia beat a British detachment under Major Gardiner near Gray's Hill. [T13]

events.name: Prevost before Charleston
events.text: Prevost's army reaches the Charleston lines, then breaks off and withdraws when it learns Lincoln is hurrying back. [T14]

events.name: Stono Ferry
events.text: Lincoln attacks the British rear guard at the ferry and is repulsed; both sides lose heavily. [T15]

events.name: Siege of Charleston
events.text: Clinton's army and fleet besiege the city; on 12 May Lincoln surrenders the army. [T16]

events.name: Monck's Corner
events.text: Tarleton's dragoons surprise Huger's cavalry and militia before dawn, taking horses and wagons and cutting Charleston off. [T17]

events.name: Lenud's Ferry
events.text: Tarleton surprises the American cavalry at the Santee crossing and scatters it. [T18]

events.name: Waxhaws (Buford's defeat)
events.text: Tarleton's Legion overtakes Buford's Virginians and cuts them down as they try to surrender. [T19]

events.name: Alexander's Old Field (Beckhamville)
events.text: Local Patriots beat a Loyalist party at Alexander's Old Field. Read in Morgan's list and the Archives list only. [T20]

events.name: Huck's Defeat (Williamson's Plantation)
events.text: Patriot militia surprise Captain Huck's Loyalist and British detachment; Huck is killed. [T21]

events.name: Rocky Mount
events.text: Sumter attacks the Loyalist post but cannot take it and withdraws. [T22]

events.name: Hanging Rock I (Davie's raid)
events.text: Davie's North Carolinians ambush a Loyalist party near Hanging Rock and take horses and arms. [T23]

events.name: Hanging Rock II
events.text: Sumter attacks the Loyalist camp at Hanging Rock; heavy losses on both sides, and the Americans leave without holding the post. [T24]

events.name: Cary's Fort (Sumter's raid)
events.text: Sumter's raid takes a post and a British supply convoy near the Wateree. Date uncertain: 15 Aug in the Archives list and NPS, 16-17 Aug in the ABT Fishing Creek page as Morgan read it. [T26]

events.name: Camden
events.text: Cornwallis routs Gates's army north of Camden and takes its guns and wagons. [T25]

events.name: Fishing Creek
events.text: Tarleton surprises Sumter's camp, scatters his command and retakes the convoy and prisoners. [T27]

events.name: Musgrove Mill
events.text: Patriot militia ambush and beat a Loyalist and British force at the Enoree. [T28]

events.name: Nelson's Ferry
events.text: Marion ambushes a British convoy and frees about 150 prisoners taken at Camden. Read in Morgan's list, the NPS timeline and the Archives list only. [T29]

events.name: Blue Savannah
events.text: Marion ambushes Loyalists at Blue Savannah. Read in Morgan's list, the NPS timeline and the Archives list only. [T30]

events.name: Black Mingo
events.text: Marion attacks a Loyalist camp near midnight and drives it into the swamp. [T31]

events.name: Kings Mountain
events.text: Frontier militia surround and destroy Ferguson's Loyalist force on the ridge. [T32]

events.name: Tearcoat Swamp
events.text: Marion's midnight attack routs Tynes's Loyalist camp. [T33]

events.name: Fish Dam Ford
events.text: Wemyss's night attack on Sumter's camp fails; Wemyss is wounded and taken. [T34]

events.name: Blackstock's
events.text: Tarleton attacks Sumter's position and is beaten back with heavy loss; Sumter is badly wounded. [T35]

events.name: Rugeley's Mill
events.text: Colonel Rugeley's Loyalists surrender to Washington's dragoons. Read in Morgan's list and the Archives list only (Archives dates it 1 Dec). [T36]

events.name: Halfway Swamp
events.text: Marion's men meet a large Loyalist and British party. Accounts differ on whether a fight took place. [T37]

events.name: Hammond's Store
events.text: Washington's dragoons ride down a Loyalist force sent from Georgia. [T38]

events.name: Cowpens
events.text: Morgan defeats Tarleton's British regulars. [T39]

summaries.title: 1775: the Patriots take the forts
summaries.text: The royal government loses its grip. Patriot leaders carry off the arms in Charleston, the Crown's forts at Charlotte and Johnson are given up without a fight, and in the backcountry the first bloodshed ends in a truce and then a Patriot march that breaks the Loyalist camps.

summaries.title: 1776: the fort holds, the Cherokee war
summaries.text: The palmetto fort on Sullivan's Island drives off the British fleet in June, and Breach Inlet stops the landing. The Cherokee war opens on the western frontier in July; results of the August fights are disputed.

summaries.title: 1777: a gap in the list
summaries.text: The Archives list has no action for 1777. The one thing read for the year is the end of the Cherokee war: the treaty of 20 May 1777 gives up the Lower Towns' lands.

summaries.title: 1778: one entry
summaries.text: The list has one entry for the year, the capture of privateers at Charleston on 19 Jun. Nothing read says who took them.

summaries.title: 1779: Prevost's move
summaries.text: Moultrie beats a British detachment on Port Royal Island in February. In May Prevost's army reaches the Charleston lines and withdraws when Lincoln hurries back. In June Lincoln's attack at Stono Ferry is repulsed; the sources differ on how to score it.

summaries.title: 1780: Charleston falls, then the partisan war
summaries.text: The British besiege Charleston and Lincoln surrenders on 12 May. Tarleton wins at Monck's Corner, Lenud's Ferry and the Waxhaws, and Cornwallis routs Gates at Camden in August. Local Patriot partisans (Sumter, Marion, the Over-Mountain men) win at Huck's Defeat, Musgrove Mill, Black Mingo, Kings Mountain, Tearcoat Swamp and Fish Dam Ford; Sumter is beaten at Fishing Creek.

summaries.title: 1781: Cowpens
summaries.text: On 17 Jan Morgan beats Tarleton at Cowpens. Playback ends here; the later actions are loaded as data only.

summaries.title: Where things stood on 17 January 1781
summaries.text: The British hold Charleston and the posts inland; Patriot partisans hold the swamps and the backcountry, and Morgan's win at Cowpens has opened Greene's campaign. Who held which place is drawn from the control rows, several of them low confidence.

clashes.place: Charleston (State House, Broad and Meeting Streets)
clashes.result: Arms and powder taken from the State House and two magazines, no fight
clashes.captured: About 800 muskets and other arms from the State House attic; about 1,600 lb of powder from the Hobcaw and Cochran's magazines

location.basis: Taken at town level from the infobox coordinate of the Siege of Charleston article (S121); the State House stood at the northwest corner of Broad and Meeting Streets (S117), about 2 km south-southeast of that point, and the powder magazines lay across the Cooper River (Hobcaw) and north of the town (Cochran's). To be read from a modern map.

clashes.notes: Cross-checked: S116 (list no. 1) and S117 (place, quantities). No second source gives the quantities.

clashes.result: Fort surrendered without a fight

location.basis: Taken from the GPS of the Fort Charlotte memorial site on the lake shore (S126); the marker on Route 81 at Mt. Carmel (34.0059, -82.5072) says the ruins lie 6.6 miles southwest of it (HMdb 9185, S122). The ruins lie under the lake, so the true point is within about 2 km.

clashes.notes: Cross-checked: S116 (list no. 3), HMdb marker 9185 (Mayson seized it 12 Jul 1775; Whitfield surrendered it) (peaceful surrender).

clashes.result: Fort taken without a fight after the navy disabled its guns
clashes.captured: The fort (the British had disabled its guns)

location.basis: The coordinates ABT gives for Fort Johnson (Fort Johnson Rd, northeast point of James Island, S120); Lipscomb places the fort on Windmill Point (S117).

clashes.notes: Cross-checked: S117 (the navy disabled the guns; Motte entered; three privates left; no fighting) and the ABT heritage-site page (Motte took it with little resistance). The ABT page gives no day; The Archives list gives 15 Sep.

clashes.place: Savage's Old Field / Williamson's fort, Ninety Six
clashes.result: Loyalists besiege Williamson's camp; a truce ends it

other.text: The NPS timeline dates the siege 10-21 Nov 1775 and the park brochure puts the first attack on 18 Nov; the Archives list, Wikipedia and the NPS anniversary page say 19-21 Nov. All sources read agree on the result: no winner and a truce.

location.basis: The knoll in Ninety Six National Historic Site where the 1775 stockade stood (NPS online tour stop 16 and the Colonials and Patriots survey, S128); Wikipedia's infobox coordinate for the site (S121); HMdb 30623 marker at 34.1469, -82.0232 (S122).

clashes.notes: Loss: Patriots 1 killed 12 wounded, Loyalists 4 killed 20 wounded (S121, citing Cann, SCHM 76, pp. 207-214). Date disagreement only; result agreed. Dagger on the date.

clashes.place: Great Cane Brake (Reedy River, near Simpsonville)
clashes.result: Loyalist camp surprised; about 130 taken
clashes.captured: About 130 Loyalists, with men, weapons and supplies

location.basis: The marker stands at the Wikipedia coordinate (S121); the marker text puts the fight along the south side of a creek running to the Reedy River and its present place on Fork Shoals Road is not the original (HMdb 97258, S122). The exact ground is not known.

clashes.notes: Cross-checked: S116 (list no. 11), S125 and Wikipedia (5 or 6 Loyalists killed, 1 Patriot wounded, about 130 captured), S123 (Richardson entry: an unquestioned success).

clashes.result: Fort holds; the fleet fails to force the harbour

location.basis: The coordinate of Fort Moultrie (S121, from NPS); the 1776 palmetto fort stood on Sullivan's Island at the harbour mouth (S119; Lipscomb S117).

clashes.notes: Cross-checked by S117, S119 (first decisive Patriot victory over the Royal Navy; British over 200 casualties, Americans 12 killed 26 wounded), S120 (American Victory) and S118. Ship mark: British ships.

clashes.result: Landing attempt stopped at the inlet

location.basis: HMdb 67277 marker on Sullivan's Island at Breach Inlet, 32 46.487 N 79 48.868 W (S122); the American lines stood on the island side and the British camp on Long Island (Isle of Palms).

clashes.notes: Cross-checked: S119 (Clinton's flotilla could not cross against Thomson's fire; the inlet was far deeper than he believed), S117 (no usable ford), S120 (label American Victory; read from a search result only).

clashes.result: Ambush on Williamson's column; the Patriots recover and drive the force off (proposed)

other.text: The NPS timeline says only that the Patriots were ambushed by Cherokees and rescued by a mounted charge, and the SC Encyclopedia says Cameron's force ambushed Williamson. ABT scores it an American victory.

location.basis: The HMdb Seneca Town / Fort Rutledge marker near Clemson (34 40.013 N, 82 50.708 W, S122); the town lay on the east side of the Keowee River and is now under Lake Hartwell (ABT, Liberty Trail). The town's exact place is lost.

clashes.notes: PROPOSED reading only (ABT). Needs Opus: see SCH02. Black (Cherokee) is not drawn unless the other reading is adopted as a Cherokee win, which no source read says.

clashes.result: Pickens's ring holds until relief; the Cherokee flee and Tamassee is burned (proposed)

other.text: ABT scores the Ring Fight inconclusive and the Liberty Trail says it had no victors; the SC Encyclopedia counts 65 Cherokee killed against 11 of Pickens's men.

location.basis: The Tamassee Town marker at the road junction near the site (HMQ2V, 34 52.98 N 83 2.91 W; text: "near this site", S122).

clashes.notes: PROPOSED reading only. Not on Morgan's dagger list: this session found the disagreement. Needs Opus: see SCH03.

clashes.place: Port Royal Island, near Gray's Hill
clashes.result: Moultrie beats a British detachment; it withdraws

location.basis: HMdb 14738 marker near the old halfway house at Gray's Hill (32 28.849 N 80 44.387 W, S122); the marker stands about 6 miles north of Beaufort (S122); Wikipedia gives 32.5003, -80.7436 (S121).

clashes.notes: Cross-checked: ABT American Victory (casualties not re-read), NPS timeline (Moultrie defeated a British detachment), SC Encyclopedia entry.

clashes.result: Prevost's advance on the city ends in a withdrawal

location.basis: The infobox coordinate of the Siege of Charleston article (S121), used for the line of the city's defences; the British reached the lines on 11-12 May and were found gone on 13 May (S124, S118).

clashes.notes: No battle was won: the British broke off on 12-13 May when Lincoln was found to be returning (S118, S124). Drawn as an American success because the city held.

clashes.result: Lincoln's attack on the rear guard repulsed (proposed)

other.text: The NPS timeline calls it inconclusive but costly to both sides; ABT scores it a British victory and the NPS siege article says Lincoln was repulsed.

location.basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate (S121) .

clashes.notes: PROPOSED reading only. Casualties (Wikipedia): Americans 34 killed, 113 wounded, 155 missing; British 26 killed, 93 wounded, 1 missing. Needs Opus: see SCH04.

clashes.result: City and army surrendered 12 May
clashes.captured: Charleston and the American army: about 5,000 men (5,266 to 5,466 by the figures Wikipedia gives), 311 guns, 49 ships and 120 boats

other.text: Same result, different start date: ABT begins the siege on 11 Feb 1780 (the landing); the NPS timeline, Wikipedia and Mount Vernon begin it on 29 Mar (the crossing of the Ashley).

location.basis: The infobox coordinate of the Siege of Charleston article (S121) (about the Neck and the lines of 1780); the city centre lies about 2 km south-southeast.

clashes.notes: Cross-checked by Britannica (Lincoln surrendered 12 May), NPS timeline, ABT map page and Wikipedia (Buchanan pp. 26-29; Borick p. 169; Mattern p. 101). Fort Moultrie surrendered 7 May without a fight. Ship mark: British fleet crossed the bar on 8 Apr. Date dagger only.

clashes.result: American cavalry and militia scattered before dawn
clashes.captured: 185 horses and 30 wagons of arms, powder, clothing and ammunition

location.basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate (S121); ABT places it at Monck's Corner, Berkeley County.

clashes.notes: The "Not checked" row, now read: ABT (British Victory; American 15 killed, 18 wounded, 63 missing or captured; British 3 wounded) and Wikipedia (Ward 1952; Wilson 2005).

clashes.result: American cavalry surprised at the ferry and scattered
clashes.captured: About 100 horses, arms and equipment; 18 British prisoners freed

location.basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate near Jamestown (S121); ABT places it at the crossing of the Santee River in Berkeley County.

clashes.notes: The "Not checked" row, now read: ABT (British Victory; about 41 American casualties, none British), Wikipedia (Buchanan pp. 68-69; Borick p. 193).

clashes.result: Buford's command destroyed

location.basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate near Lancaster County (S121).

clashes.notes: Cross-checked: NPS (113 bayoneted), Wikipedia (113 killed, 150 wounded, 53 captured; Piecuch).

clashes.result: Sumter's attack fails; he withdraws (proposed)
clashes.captured: Nothing at the post; Sumter claimed about 60 Loyalists, a few horses and some supplies on the retreat

other.text: Wikipedia dates the action 31 Jul or 1 Aug, against 30 Jul in the Archives list, the NPS timeline and ABT; the result agrees (British victory, ABT and Wikipedia; Sumter withdrew, NPS).

location.basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate (S121).

clashes.notes: Result as ABT (via Morgan's list) and Wikipedia: British victory. The captured-by line is Sumter's own claim as Morgan's list gives it. Date dagger.

clashes.result: Davie's raid on the Loyalist camp succeeds
clashes.captured: 60 horses and about 100 muskets and rifles

other.text: Wikipedia dates Davie's raid 1 Aug; the Archives list, the NPS timeline and ABT (as a diversion for Rocky Mount) date it 30 Jul. Same result.

location.basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate for the Hanging Rock action (S121); Davie's raid was on the Loyalist camp in the same district (ABT, Heath Springs).

clashes.notes: Date dagger only (SCH06). The quantities are as Morgan's list gives them (from the Archives list); Wikipedia says 60 horses and some weapons.

clashes.result: Heavy losses on both sides; Sumter leaves the field (proposed)
clashes.captured: About 100 horses, 250 stands of arms and 73 prisoners (Sumter's report, as ABT quotes it)

other.text: NPS: Sumter inflicted heavy casualties but was forced to retreat; Wikipedia: American victory with the Americans leaving the field; ABT: American Victory though Sumter did not take the garrison.

location.basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate (S121); ABT places it at the garrison on the Camden to Charlotte road at Heath Springs.

clashes.notes: PROPOSED reading only. Casualties (ABT): Americans 53, British 200; Sumter's own letter gives other figures. Needs Opus: see SCH07.

clashes.result: Gates's army routed
clashes.captured: All 8 American guns, over 200 wagons; about 1,000 prisoners (Cornwallis)

location.basis: The coordinates ABT gives for the Camden battlefield (S120); Wikipedia 34.3646, -80.6139 (S121).

clashes.notes: The "Not checked" row, now read: ABT (British Victory; casualty figures not re-read), Wikipedia (Ramsay vol. 2 p. 169 for guns, wagons and baggage; Cornwallis to Germain, 21 Aug, for the prisoners).

clashes.place: Fishing Creek, north of Great Falls
clashes.result: Sumter's camp surprised and his command scattered
clashes.captured: About 300 American prisoners; wagons, artillery pieces, about 800 horses and about 1,000 weapons (ABT, as Morgan's list reads it); the British prisoners and baggage Sumter had taken

location.basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate (S121), north of Great Falls in Chester County.

clashes.notes: Cross-checked: NPS (Tarleton surprised and defeated Sumter), Wikipedia (British victory; about 300 captured; Pancake), Morgan's list for the ABT page (guns, horses, weapons counts not re-read).

clashes.result: Loyalist force ambushed and beaten; Patriots then withdraw

other.text: Same result, two dates: 18 Aug (NPS, the Archives list, Wikipedia's infobox) against 19 Aug (ABT, Wikipedia's lead).

location.basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate for the state historic site (S121).

clashes.notes: Loyalists 63 killed and 70 captured; Patriots 4 killed and 12 wounded (wayside, via Wikipedia). Edgar pp. 130-38; Buchanan pp. 177-179. Date dagger only.

clashes.result: Loyalist camp attacked at midnight and driven into the swamp

location.basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate, given to the minute (S121).

clashes.notes: The attack came near midnight on 28/29 Sep (Wikipedia infobox 28, text 29; Crawford 2024 p. 116 for the date). Patriots 2 killed, 8 wounded.

clashes.result: Ferguson's force destroyed
clashes.captured: About 698 British and Loyalists missing and captured (ABT, via Morgan's list); Wikipedia gives 668 or 698

location.basis: Wikipedia's infobox coordinate (S121); the battlefield is a National Military Park.

clashes.notes: Cross-checked: NPS (frontier militia surrounded and defeated Ferguson, a decisive Patriot victory), Wikipedia (the article cites Dameron and Buchanan; pages not recorded). The capture figures differ: 668 or 698.

clashes.notes: Cross-checked: NPS (Marion routed Tynes), ABT (American Victory; 43 casualties, all Loyalist), carolana (6 killed, 14 wounded, 23 captured), HMdb. Boatner places it near where US 301 crosses the Black River.

other.text: The NPS timeline says Marion engaged a larger Loyalist group, which retreated, and that a trap at Singleton's Mill failed; the 2010 Clarendon County marker says the British agreed to a staged fight of twenty men each but slipped away overnight, so there was no full battle.

places.name: Charleston (Charles Town)

places.name: Ninety Six
